findings.title: Render controlled stops even when delivery evidence cannot be hashed
findings.claim: The final route computes validationSnapshot before rendering pendingStop. The runner sends snapshot failures to this same final route, so those controlled stops have no usable HTTP confirmation page.
findings.impact: An admitted screen that is missing, an unreadable passed audit report, or malformed UI JSON causes /final to return 409 instead of the stop explanation and Confirm/resume button. The saved run keeps pendingStop and each subsequent invocation returns the same unusable URL until the underlying evidence is repaired externally.
reproduction: Create plan.md with a passed phase citing a nonempty audit.md, flow/flow.html, and ui/ui.json containing screens:[{path:'ui/missing.html'}]; do not create that screen.
Start serveFlowHtml(flowHtml,{planPath:plan}), then call runPlanEndWorkflow with preview returning that server URL.
The workflow returns {action:'stop',reason:'não avanço',url:'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/final?stop=...'} without invoking a reviewer.
Fetch outcome.url: observed HTTP 409 with ENOENT lstat .../ui/missing.html. There is no confirmation form or token.
findings.evidence: Runner scripts/automate-run.js:908-909 catches the snapshot failure and saves pendingStop; GET /final calls the same snapshot unconditionally at scripts/lib/serve-flow.js:120. Existing runtime missing-ui-screen test only fetches server.url (/flow.html), leaving this failure untested.
findings.recommendation: Allow a stop-only presentation and confirmation token to bind to the exact saved pendingStop id and runtime identity when delivered evidence is unavailable. Keep same-origin POST and matching token/cookie checks, reject a stale token after the pending stop changes, and keep the delivery-validation button disabled with its full snapshot requirements.

findings.title: Handle Git submodule entries before reading tracked product bytes
findings.claim: git ls-files lists an initialized submodule as its gitlink directory, but productSnapshot treats every entry as an ordinary file and calls readFileSync on that directory.
findings.impact: Any initialized tracked submodule in a target repository makes productSnapshot throw EISDIR. Whole-plan review cannot begin, and the HTTP final page also fails because both validationSnapshot and rendering call productSnapshot.
reproduction: Initialize a Git repository with plan.md and a commit; create an existing vendor directory representing an initialized submodule.
Add its Gitlink using git update-index --add --cacheinfo 160000,<valid-commit-sha>,vendor, or use a normal git submodule add.
Call productSnapshot(planPath). Observed EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read.
findings.evidence: src/plan-end-review.js:548 obtains paths without Git entry modes, and lines 551-557 read existing paths as files. A Gitlink is mode 160000 and resolves to a directory when initialized.
findings.recommendation: Read tracked entries with their modes, hash each gitlink commit identity, and explicitly define how changed submodule contents invalidate reviews. Add a real initialized-submodule regression case.

manualReproductions: controlled stop returns /final URL whose GET is HTTP 409 ENOENT
productSnapshot with tracked existing gitlink directory throws EISDIR

limitations: Bounded to F5 completion paths; unrelated F4 phase driver was not audited.
The workspace HEAD changed concurrently after source inspection; findings bind to the requested sourceHead.
